description: Weaponsmith. She hands every blade over hilt-first and watches how you take it — that is her deciding which of the trade's two words you are.
lore: What was left of her husband walked. A [[lore/the_quiet|Habit]] shape runs one faithful loop, empty of anyone; his ran the roads he had walked home by all his life, and it ended at her door, and stood there, and did not knock. She let it stand the first time. By the third she understood what a shape on open road is to any stranger with a good eye and a day to spare. So she opened the door and let him finish arriving — all the way in, all the way home — and broke the shape herself, at the hearth, with the doors shut.

The hammer she uses now she made in the days between — a new head with a socket sunk in it, sized to a [[lore/the_hard_pieces|stone]] she did not yet hold. Practical people grieve forward. What rides in that socket is the trade's favourite story and not one she tells; what she will do is pass the finished blade across hilt-first and watch how it gets taken. Some people receive a sword. Some people take one. She has lifted a blade back out of a buyer's grip and returned the gold without explanation, and the trade has learned not to ask.

He says she is the best teacher he never asked for. She has heard him say it and let it stand, which from her is a great deal. [[characters/54bead23|Osric]] arrived weeks-woken with the living word for breaking things still in his mouth, and she took it off him inside a month — not by correcting him, but by making him watch her work until the wrong word embarrassed itself. He says she is the best teacher he never asked for, and she has let the sentence stand, which from her is a great deal. As for the name she has not said since that day at the hearth: it is not in this record, it is not in the Chronicle, and it is not going to be. She is not keeping it from anyone. She is keeping it.
gm_notes: Carries B11 (revealed). The name (GM: it is Stig) NEVER ships — not here, not anywhere — until the scene where she says it; printing it first wastes her best moment. New leaf-canon here: the release itself (the loop ending at her door, letting him finish arriving, the hearth, the socket forged in advance) and the Osric apprenticeship. the_hard_pieces owns the two-words framing and the stone-in-hammer fact — never restate its sentences. tree_stump holds her Stumpling exception; related joins them.
